unit.why: A short anecdote about the Ari, quoted from Hiddushei ha-Rim within a homily on visiting the sick: the Ari rose before a man, and Vital asked why. It is a narrative about a pre-Hasidic kabbalist.
unit.boundary_note: anecdote embedded in a homiletic discussion that runs from the previous division into the next

stories.start_quote: וכניו שאמר האר"י ז"ל שבא מהר"ש
stories.summary_en: The Ari stood up and showed great honour to a visiting man; when R. Hayyim Vital asked why, he explained that the man had performed a mitzvah that R. Pinhas ben Yair used to do, so the tanna's soul had joined him to help, and it was before that soul that the Ari rose.

tags.why: praises the Ari's supernatural insight; the story is quoted from an earlier book
the anecdote is wrapped in a homily on visiting the sick and on the soul of Abraham
the Ari perceives the tanna's soul accompanying the man
a soul attaches to a living person (ibbur), which is close to gilgul
the hidden reason for the honour is revealed afterwards

missing_concepts: ibbur (impregnation of a living person by a righteous soul) through performing a mitzvah
